en: The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
The Training Rule on Swinging the Arms.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks walked through inhabited areas swinging their arms and letting them hang down...
[as before]... "The training is to be observed: 'I will not walk through an inhabited area swinging my arms.
One must not walk through an inhabited area swinging one's arms."
One should go with one’s arm held up.
Whoever, out of disrespect, goes among the houses swinging his arms or letting his arms hang down, commits an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
"Unintentionally... [as before] ...for one who is a first-time offender.
The seventh training rule is concluded.
